Cm Appl. 26705/2025 [Condonation of delay]
1.  This is an Application filed on behalf of the Appellants seeking condonation of delay of 168 days in filing the present Appeal.

2. Learned Counsel for the Appellants submits that the Appellants belong to a poor strata of the society and in view of the untimely death of the deceased pursuant to the accident, the Appellants have suffered severe financial hardships, since the deceased was the sole breadwinner of the family.

It is further stated that it took some time for the Appellants to find the funds to take legal action,
and thus, there is a delay.
It is stated that the delay is neither intentional nor deliberate.
3. For the reasons as stated in the Application, the delay is condoned.
4. The Application stands disposed of.

6. The Application stands disposed of.

The present Appeal has been filed on behalf of the Appellants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award and judgment dated 16.07.2024 [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"] passed by learned Presiding Officer, MACT-01, South West District, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi.

sentences.text: 7.1 The challenge in the present Appeal is for enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded in the sum of Rs.2,31,000/- along with 9% interest per annum.
8. Learned Counsel for the Appellants submits that the deceased suffered severe injuries in the accident and sustained a permanent physical disability of 75% in his left lower limb.
It is submitted that the deceased was under continuous treatment for 21 months, and thereafter, he passed away.

It is submitted that the cause of death of the deceased was in view of the amputation and other grievous injuries sustained in the accident, however, the learned Tribunal has not taken this fact into account.
9. Issue Notice.
9.1 Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.3 accepts Notice.
9.2 Learned Counsel for the parties submit that service to Respondent Nos.1 and 2 may be dispensed with.
